en.title: Maximum Covered Population with Each Security Unit Moving Left At Most Once
en.description:
Cities are arranged in a row, and unit[i]=1 means a unit is initially there. A unit may stay or move once to the adjacent city on its left; a unit in the first city can only stay. In the end, a city with at least one unit contributes population[i] once; overlapping units do not contribute again. Find the maximum protected population.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line population, and the third line a 01 string unit of length n. The original text only kept the constraint that the two arrays have equal length, with no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, 0≤population[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 27, 7 and 101. In the third example two units cannot count the 100 in the middle twice.
hints: Run a DP from left to right with two states: whether the previous city has a unit staying there. Once you decide whether the current unit stays or moves left, the final coverage of the previous city is fixed, so settle its population; finally settle the last city.
